title: MongoDB Search
description: mongot behind the operator-managed Envoy: is it up, is traffic spread, is Envoy healthy.

panels.title: Is search up?
mongot pods up
panels.description: mongot pods that Prometheus scrapes successfully.

panels.title: Envoy pods up
panels.description: Envoy pods that Prometheus scrapes successfully.

panels.title: mongot pods in Envoy
panels.description: The smallest number of healthy mongot pods any Envoy pod sees. Below the number of mongot pods, an Envoy pod has lost one.

panels.title: Searches per second
panels.description: Text and vector searches per second, all mongot pods, 5 minute rate.

panels.title: Largest share on one pod
panels.description: The share of all searches that the busiest mongot pod served. With three pods and even balancing this is about 33%. Near 100% means one pod serves everything while the others stay Ready: the failure that produces no error. 0% when no search ran in the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: Is traffic spread across the mongot pods?
Searches per second, per mongot pod
panels.description: Stacked: one band per mongot pod, and the top edge is all searches. Envoy picks a mongot pod per request, so the bands should be of equal height. 5 minute rate.

panels.title: Share of searches, per mongot pod
panels.description: Stacked: each pod's part of all searches over the last 5 minutes, adding up to 100%. Three pods sharing evenly are three bands of a third each.

panels.title: Share of searches now, by mongot pod
panels.description: Each pod's part of the searches of the last 5 minutes. Three equal slices is even balancing; one slice taking the pie is the failure that produces no error. Empty when no search ran.

panels.title: Responses per second from mongot, by class
panels.description: 2xx is success. gRPC errors still answer 200; see the search failures panel. 5 minute rate.

panels.title: Envoy to mongot latency, 95th percentile
panels.description: Time Envoy waited for mongot, across both Envoy pods, over the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: How is each mongot pod doing?
Average search latency, per mongot pod
panels.description: Text searches only, averaged over 5 minutes. An average hides the slowest searches: mongot exposes no latency buckets, only its own quantiles per pod (0.5 to 0.99), which this panel does not draw. No line while a pod serves none.

panels.title: Search failures per second, per mongot pod
panels.description: Text and vector searches that mongot failed, 5 minute rate.

panels.title: Replication lag, per mongot pod
panels.description: How far the pod's most delayed index is behind the source replica set.

panels.title: JVM memory used, per mongot pod
panels.description: Heap and non-heap together.

panels.title: CPU used, per mongot pod
panels.description: mongot's own CPU use, averaged over 5 minutes, as a share of the CPUs the process sees (mongot_system_cpu_count; with a CPU limit of 1 that is one core).

panels.title: JVM heap used, percent of limit, per mongot pod
panels.description: Heap in use against the heap's maximum. The panel above shows heap and non-heap together, in bytes.

panels.title: Time in garbage collection, per mongot pod
panels.description: Share of time the JVM spent paused for garbage collection, 5 minute rate.

panels.title: Uptime, per mongot pod
panels.description: Time since the mongot process started. A fall to zero is a restart.

panels.title: Search work run outside the parallel pool, per mongot pod
panels.description: Tasks per second (5 minute rate) that found mongot's concurrent search or vector rescoring pool full and ran on the calling thread instead. The search is still answered; above zero, the pool is saturated.

panels.title: Does every mongot pod hold the same data?
Each mongot pod, now
panels.description: One row per mongot pod, its name on its colour in the charts. Every pod holds every index, so the first four columns should read the same on every row.

panels.title: Index size, per mongot pod
panels.description: Bytes of all search and vector indexes on the pod. Every pod holds every index, so the lines should sit close together; each pod merges its own segments, so they need not be equal.

panels.title: Documents indexed, per mongot pod
panels.description: Documents in all indexes on the pod. Equal on every pod once each has caught up with mongod.

panels.title: Indexes not STEADY, per mongot pod
panels.description: Indexes whose state is anything but STEADY: INITIAL_SYNC, STALE, FAILED, RECOVERING and the rest. Should be 0; above it, that pod's copy of an index is not ready.

panels.title: Indexes in catalog, per mongot pod
panels.description: How many indexes each pod knows about. The same on every pod.

panels.title: Data volume used, per mongot pod
panels.description: Used share of the file system under mongot's data path, as mongot reports it. With a volume of its own per pod this is that volume; with a hostpath provisioner it is the node's disk, the same on every pod.

panels.title: Indexing operations per second, per mongot pod
panels.description: Inserts, updates and deletes applied to the indexes, 5 minute rate. Every pod applies the same changes, so the lines should move together.
